column1: # 66-guard-expectations.tsv: what every guard must read. Read by 66-guard-summary.py.
# One row per guard heading, tab separated:
#   slot <TAB> guard key <TAB> source <TAB> distilled <TAB> reason
# slot       the number of the output file (30-38, 41, 42, ...); for script 39 the number
# guard key  the heading text before its first ": ", " (" or " = ". Run
#            66-guard-summary.py <label> --propose to print the key of every heading
#            that has no row yet, with a first guess.
# source     what the guard must read on a source backup, before reject and repair.
# distilled  what it must read on the new database, after reject and repair.
#   zero              every number in the block is 0 (a block with no rows passes)
#   zero-but:<text>   the same, rows whose first cell holds <text> are left out
#   empty             the block has no rows at all
#   cells:a=0,b=t     every row reads these values in the named columns
#   row:<text>:a=0    the rows whose first cell holds <text> read this value in column a
#   equals:<n>        the block is one cell and it reads <n>
#   head:<n>          the heading itself carries the value after " = " (script 41)
#   match:<regex>     one line of the block matches
#   a ; b             several checks, all must pass (space, semicolon, space)
#   baseline          no fixed value: compared with the stored baseline of the label,
#                     reported SAME or MOVED, never FAIL
#   as-source         distilled only: the reading equals the reading of the same guard on the
#                     source backup (--source <label>). For guards the copy and the repairs
#                     must not move. FAIL when it differs
#   agreed            distilled only: the reading equals the agreed reading stored for this
#                     dataset (66-baselines/<label>.distilled.tsv). For guards that the copy or
#                     a repair moves to a value that depends on the data. FAIL when it differs,
#                     NO BASELINE on a new dataset until a person has read it and saved it
#   open:<text>       a known open item: reported OPEN, never PASS. <text> names the work
#   undecided         nobody has ruled what it must read. Reported UNDECIDED
#   info | section    reported only; the heading must still be present
#   note              the heading is a comment line of the guard before it
# A heading in the output with no row here is a FAIL line. So is a row here whose
# heading is not in the output. A new guard therefore needs a new row.
# @slot lines: required = the run fails without the file; the other words say why a
# missing file is only reported as NOT RUN.
